1_parties_and_buyer_credit.value: Seller is Havrebakke Vind ApS and Buyer is Jutland Board & Packaging A/S, both Danish companies. The Buyer's payment obligations are guaranteed by Jutland Industri Holding A/S under a Parent Company Guarantee (Annex 4). The Buyer has no credit rating from a recognised agency. There is no rating trigger. The replacement trigger in section 9.5 applies if the Guarantor ceases to hold all of the Buyer's share capital or the guarantee ceases to be in force.
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.quote: The Buyer's payment obligations under this Agreement are guaranteed by Jutland Industri Holding A/S under the Parent Company Guarantee set out in Annex 4.
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.clause: Part I, Parties; Annex 4; sections 9.2 and 9.5
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.note: The document is a draft, subject to contract and not binding until signed. Annex 4 is an unsigned form with the date left blank. Its liability is capped only at the Buyer's own liability (Annex 4, para 5).

2_facility.value: Onshore wind farm of eight turbines (6.0 MW each) with total installed capacity of 48.0 MW. It is located at Havrebakke, Ringkøbing-Skjern Municipality, Denmark, in bidding zone DK1.
2_facility.quote: The Facility is the Havrebakke Wind Farm, consisting of eight onshore wind turbine generators with a total installed capacity of 48.0 MW located at Havrebakke in Ringkøbing-Skjern Municipality, Denmark, in bidding zone DK1, together with the internal cabling, the Havrebakke substation and the ancillary installations described in Annex 1.
2_facility.note: Only one capacity figure is given. There is no AC/DC split, which is not relevant for wind.

3_supply_period.value: Ten years, starting on the Commercial Operation Date. The Commercial Operation Date is the date the Seller notifies the Buyer that the section 3.3 conditions are met (all eight turbines commissioned, grid connected at the Delivery Point, meters verified, registrations done).
3_supply_period.quote: Supply Period: ten (10) years commencing on the Commercial Operation Date.
3_supply_period.clause: Part I, Supply Period; section 1.1 (Commercial Operation Date); section 3.3
3_supply_period.note: The start is triggered by the Seller's own notice. The Buyer is given at least 30 days' notice of the expected date.

4_cod_and_delay.value: Target Commercial Operation Date is 1 October 2027 and Longstop Date is 31 December 2027. Delay liquidated damages are EUR 9,600 per day, capped at EUR 1,750,000 in aggregate. Both dates extend day for day for Force Majeure or Buyer breach, up to 180 days in aggregate. If the Longstop Date passes, the Buyer may terminate with no Termination Amount. The Seller pays accrued unpaid liquidated damages.
4_cod_and_delay.quote: If the Commercial Operation Date has not occurred by the Target Commercial Operation Date of 1 October 2027, the Seller shall pay the Buyer liquidated damages of EUR 9,600 for each day of delay, up to an aggregate cap of EUR 1,750,000.
4_cod_and_delay.clause: Part I, Supply Period; section 1.1 (Longstop Date); sections 3.4 to 3.6
4_cod_and_delay.note: Calculated from the stated figures, not stated in the document: the window from target to longstop is 91 days, which is about EUR 873,600 of liquidated damages. The cap equals roughly 182 days of delay, so it cannot be reached before the Longstop Date. The Buyer's termination right under 3.6 arises at the Longstop Date, as extended under 3.5.

5_price_and_indexation.value: Fixed price of EUR 58.00 per MWh, exclusive of VAT, for each MWh of Metered Output from the Commercial Operation Date. There is no indexation and the price is fixed for the whole Supply Period.
5_price_and_indexation.quote: Contract Price: EUR 58.00 per MWh, exclusive of value added tax, applicable to each MWh of Metered Output from the Commercial Operation Date.
5_price_and_indexation.clause: Annex 2 (Election Sheet), referred to by Part I, Price and section 7.1
5_price_and_indexation.note: The price sits only in Annex 2, not in Part I or the body. The indexation statement is also in Annex 2: 'Indexation: none. The Contract Price is fixed for the Supply Period and shall not be indexed.' Section 11.2 allows a Change in Law price adjustment by negotiation. See term 12 for how that fits with Annex 2 being the exclusive source of price adjustment.

6_volume_and_performance.value: Pay-as-produced: the Buyer takes 100% of Metered Output. Expected Annual Production is 158,000 MWh (P50). The Minimum Annual Production guarantee is 118,500 MWh (75% of P50). If output falls short in a Contract Year, the Seller pays shortfall MWh times the positive excess of the average DK1 day-ahead price over the Contract Price, capped at EUR 500,000 per Contract Year. The minimum is reduced pro rata in the first and last Contract Year and for Force Majeure, TSO-instructed reductions and Buyer breach.
6_volume_and_performance.quote: If in any Contract Year the Metered Output is less than the Minimum Annual Production, the Seller shall pay the Buyer a shortfall payment equal to the shortfall in MWh multiplied by the amount, if positive, by which the average day-ahead price for bidding zone DK1 for that Contract Year exceeds the Contract Price, capped at EUR 500,000 per Contract Year.
6_volume_and_performance.clause: Part I, Contract Quantity and Volume Structure; Annex 1; Annex 2; sections 4.1, 4.3, 4.5, 4.6
6_volume_and_performance.note: The remedy is a price-based payment and is nil in years when the day-ahead price is at or below EUR 58.00. The Seller gives no guarantee for any hour, day or month (4.3).

7_product_and_certificates.value: The Seller sells electricity delivered at the Delivery Point together with all Guarantees of Origin for the Metered Output. The Guarantees of Origin are transferred at no additional cost, monthly, within 15 Business Days after issue. Certificates under a replacement scheme are also transferred at no additional cost. No capacity product, ancillary service or other attribute is sold.
7_product_and_certificates.quote: All Guarantees of Origin issued in respect of the Metered Output shall be transferred to the Buyer at no additional cost.
7_product_and_certificates.clause: Part I, Product and Certificates; section 8
7_product_and_certificates.note: The Seller has no obligation to procure replacement Guarantees of Origin for a production shortfall (8.2).

8_curtailment.value: The only curtailment addressed is output reductions instructed by the transmission system operator. These give rise to no payment by the Buyer, so curtailed energy is not paid as deemed delivery. Any compensation paid by the TSO belongs to the Seller. TSO-instructed reductions (and Force Majeure and Buyer breach) reduce the Minimum Annual Production for the shortfall test, using the deemed quantity calculation in 5.5.
8_curtailment.quote: Reductions of output instructed by the transmission system operator shall not give rise to any payment by the Buyer.
8_curtailment.note: The document has no provision on curtailment by the Buyer, no cap in hours or MWh, and no treatment of negative prices (I read the full document for these). Deemed quantities are used only to adjust the minimum production test, not to pay the Seller.

9_delivery_point_and_balancing.value: Physical settlement. The Delivery Point is the metering point on the 60 kV side of the Havrebakke substation, where title and risk pass to the Buyer. The Buyer appoints the balance responsible party and bears all imbalance costs from the Commercial Operation Date. No financial reference price applies because settlement is physical.
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.quote: The Buyer shall appoint the balance responsible party for the Facility and shall bear all imbalance costs from the Commercial Operation Date.
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.clause: Part I, Settlement and Delivery Point and Balancing; Annex 2; sections 4.2 and 5.2
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.note: The Seller must supply day-ahead and intraday forecasts to the balance responsible party, without warranty (5.1).

10_credit_support.value: Seller: bank guarantee of EUR 2,000,000 from a bank rated at least A-, delivered within 10 Business Days after Financial Close and valid until 12 months after the Commercial Operation Date. Buyer: the Parent Company Guarantee plus a standby letter of credit from a bank rated at least A-, sized at six months of expected payments (six twelfths of Expected Annual Production times the Contract Price). It is delivered at least 30 days before the expected Commercial Operation Date, valid until 60 days after the end of the Supply Period, and recalculated each 1 January.
10_credit_support.quote: The Seller shall deliver a bank guarantee in the amount of EUR 2,000,000 within ten (10) Business Days after Financial Close, to remain in force until twelve (12) months after the Commercial Operation Date.
10_credit_support.clause: Part I, Credit Support; section 9; Annexes 3 and 4
10_credit_support.note: The Buyer letter of credit has no stated figure. Calculated from the formula at EUR 58.00 and 158,000 MWh, it is about EUR 4.58 million. Section 9.5 requires a replacement guarantee or double the letter of credit if the Guarantor ceases to own the Buyer or the guarantee lapses.

11_default_and_termination.value: Events of default: non-payment (10 Business Days after notice); failure to deliver, restore or replace credit support (10 Business Days); insolvency; uncured material breach (30 days); breach of the assignment rules; for the Seller, no Commercial Operation Date by the Longstop Date or sale to a third party; for the Buyer, Guarantor insolvency or the guarantee ceasing to be valid. The Termination Amount is the present value of the difference between the Contract Price and the Reference Forward Price over the remainder of the Supply Period for Expected Annual Production. It is discounted at the central bank reference rate plus 2 percentage points and determined by the Non-Defaulting Party. It is payable only if it is a loss for the Non-Defaulting Party.
11_default_and_termination.quote: The Termination Amount shall be the present value of the difference between the Contract Price and the Reference Forward Price for the Expected Annual Production over the remainder of the Supply Period, discounted at the reference rate of the Danish central bank plus two (2) percentage points, and determined by the Non-Defaulting Party as at the early termination date, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner.
11_default_and_termination.clause: Sections 12.1, 13.2 to 13.6; Reference Forward Price in section 1.1; production profile factor 0.88 in Annex 2
11_default_and_termination.note: The calculation is fully defined in the attached document. The Reference Forward Price uses quotes from at least three market participants chosen by the Non-Defaulting Party, scaled by the 0.88 factor. The Termination Amount is excluded from the EUR 2,000,000 annual liability cap (14.2) and is covered by the Parent Company Guarantee.

12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.value: Change in Law is cost-neutral to neither party by default. Taxes and charges on generation and injection are borne by the Seller, and those on offtake and resale by the Buyer; a new levy follows this split and is subject to section 11 above the threshold. If a Change in Law raises a Party's cost by more than EUR 250,000 in a Contract Year, the Parties negotiate in good faith an adjustment, which may include the Contract Price. If no adjustment is agreed within 90 days of notice, the affected Party may terminate with 60 days' effect and no Termination Amount. Force Majeure lasting more than 180 consecutive days lets either Party terminate with 30 days' effect and no Termination Amount.
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.quote: If a Change in Law increases the cost to a Party of performing this Agreement by more than EUR 250,000 in any Contract Year, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith an adjustment to restore the economic balance of this Agreement, which may include an adjustment to the Contract Price.
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.note: Allocation of tax costs sits in section 17, not under the Change in Law heading. Possible conflict in the draft: Part I (Price) and section 7.1 say any price adjustment is governed exclusively by Annex 2, and Annex 2 prevails but contains no Change in Law mechanism, while 11.2 contemplates a price adjustment.
